title: Explicit pair-groupoid thickening of a quasicategory
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products, nerves, quasicategories, coherent functor categories and functor equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed universe. Let $X$ be a small set with a specified element $x_0$, and let $I$ be a small quasicategory. Let $E_X$ be the ordinary category whose objects are $X$ and whose morphism set between any ordered pair of objects is a singleton, with the unique possible identities and compositions. Write $J_X=N(E_X)$, so $(J_X)_n=X^{n+1}$ and operators delete or repeat coordinates, and put $K=I\times J_X$. Then $J_X$ is a Kan complex and $K$ is a small quasicategory. The projection $p:K\to I$ is a coherent functor equivalence with quasi-inverse $s:I\to K$ given in degree $n$ by $\sigma\mapsto(\sigma,(x_0,\ldots,x_0))$; one has $ps=\mathrm{id}_I$. There is a coherent natural equivalence $\eta:sp\to\mathrm{id}_K$ whose associated simplicial map $K\times\Delta^1\to K$ is
$$((\sigma,(y_0,\ldots,y_n)),\alpha:[n]\to[1])\longmapsto(\sigma,(z_0,\ldots,z_n)),$$
Here $z_k=x_0$ if $\alpha(k)=0$, and $z_k=y_k$ if $\alpha(k)=1$. It satisfies $p\eta=p\operatorname{pr}_K$. No filteredness assumption is imposed on $I$, and $I$ may be empty.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.1.16, opening proof paragraph, printed p.383 (2012 text), read online 2026-10-17: product with the nerve of the category having one isomorphism between each pair of objects. The specified section and coordinate homotopy are the retained agent expansion of that reduction, checked against the simplicial definitions and Scholze, Six-Functor Formalisms, Lecture II, basic facts (1) and (3), printed pp.14-15. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result; HTT archive WANTED.

proof.text: An $n$-simplex of $N(E_X)$ is a functor $[n]\to E_X$. Its objects form a list $(y_0,\ldots,y_n)$; for every such list there is exactly one functor, because each arrow and every identity/composition equation in $E_X$ is unique. Restriction along $\beta:[m]\to[n]$ sends the list to $(y_{\beta(0)},\ldots,y_{\beta(m)})$. This proves the stated coordinate description, including faces and degeneracies, directly from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Each $X^{n+1}$ and $I_n\times X^{n+1}$ is small in the fixed universe, so both $J_X$ and $K$ are small.

source.place: Lecture II, Definition 2.2 and basic facts (1), (3), (4), printed pp.14-15: simplicial and inverse-triangle definitions. Agent coordinate expansion of the opening reduction in HTT Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed p.383; HTT read online but archive WANTED.

proof.text: Verify the Kan condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] by filling a horn $h:\Lambda_i^n\to J_X$, $n\geq1$. For $n=1$ the horn specifies one endpoint; choose $x_0$ for the other endpoint, giving the required two-coordinate list. For $n\geq2$ the horn contains every vertex of $\Delta^n$: for a vertex $k$, choose a face omitting a vertex different from both $i$ and $k$, which is possible among $n+1\geq3$ vertices. Let $y_k$ be its image. The single simplex $(y_0,\ldots,y_n)$ fills the horn. Indeed any simplex of the horn is a monotone map $\gamma:[m]\to[n]$ belonging to a retained face, and its image under $h$ has vertices $y_{\gamma(0)},\ldots,y_{\gamma(m)}$; step 1 says those vertices uniquely determine its image in $J_X$. Thus the proposed filler restricts to $h$, including on all degenerate simplices. This treats outer as well as inner horns.

source.place: Lecture II, Definition 2.2 and basic facts (1), (3), (4), printed pp.14-15: simplicial and inverse-triangle definitions. Agent coordinate expansion of the opening reduction in HTT Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed p.383; HTT read online but archive WANTED.

proof.text: For an inner horn in $K=I\times J_X$, project to the two factors, fill the first projected horn using the hypothesis that $I$ is a quasicategory, and fill the second by step 2. Their ordered pair is a filler because products and their operators are degreewise, as specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Hence $K$ is a quasicategory. The projection $p$ is simplicial. The map $s$ which pairs each $\sigma\in I_n$ with the constant list $(x_0,\ldots,x_0)$ is simplicial, since restriction of a constant list is constant. Coordinatewise, $ps=\mathrm{id}_I$. Write $A=sp$ and $B=\mathrm{id}_K$.

source.place: Lecture II, Definition 2.2 and basic facts (1), (3), (4), printed pp.14-15: simplicial and inverse-triangle definitions. Agent coordinate expansion of the opening reduction in HTT Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed p.383; HTT read online but archive WANTED.

proof.text: Construct the transformation and its witnesses at once using the internal-hom formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $r=0,1,2$ and a word $w=(w_0,\ldots,w_r)$ with letters in $\{0,1\}$, define $T_w:K\times\Delta^r\to K$. In degree $n$, on $((\sigma,(y_0,\ldots,y_n)),\alpha:[n]\to[r])$, its value is $(\sigma,(z_0,\ldots,z_n))$, where $z_k=x_0$ when $w_{\alpha(k)}=0$ and $z_k=y_k$ when $w_{\alpha(k)}=1$. For every $\beta:[m]\to[n]$, both restricting this output and applying the formula to the restricted input give first coordinate $I(\beta)(\sigma)$ and $k$th second coordinate $x_0$ or $y_{\beta(k)}$ according to $w_{\alpha(\beta(k))}$. Thus each $T_w$ is a simplicial map, hence an $r$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,K)$. Restriction along $\lambda:[q]\to[r]$ gives $T_{(w_{\lambda(0)},\ldots,w_{\lambda(q)})}$ by substitution; repeated letters give the corresponding degenerate simplices.

source.place: Lecture II, Definition 2.2 and basic facts (1), (3), (4), printed pp.14-15: simplicial and inverse-triangle definitions. Agent coordinate expansion of the opening reduction in HTT Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed p.383; HTT read online but archive WANTED.

proof.text: Set $\eta=T_{(0,1)}$ and $\theta=T_{(1,0)}$. The face calculation of step 4 gives endpoints $A\to B$ and $B\to A$ respectively, and gives exactly the displayed formula in the statement for $\eta$. For $T_{(0,1,0)}$, the edges $01$, $12$, $02$ are respectively $\eta$, $\theta$, $T_{(0,0)}$; the last is the degenerate identity edge at $A$. For $T_{(1,0,1)}$ they are respectively $\theta$, $\eta$, $T_{(1,1)}$, the last being the degenerate identity at $B$. These are the two inverse-triangle witnesses required by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus $\eta$ is a coherent natural equivalence with inverse $\theta$, rather than merely a simplicial homotopy.

source.place: Lecture II, Definition 2.2 and basic facts (1), (3), (4), printed pp.14-15: simplicial and inverse-triangle definitions. Agent coordinate expansion of the opening reduction in HTT Proposition 5.3.1.16, printed p.383; HTT read online but archive WANTED.

proof.text: The formula for $T_{(0,1)}$ leaves the first coordinate $\sigma$ unchanged, in every degree and for every $\alpha$, so $p\eta=p\operatorname{pr}_K$ as simplicial maps $K\times\Delta^1\to I$. We have a quasi-inverse $s$ of $p$, with $sp\simeq\mathrm{id}_K$ supplied by step 5 and $ps=\mathrm{id}_I$ supplied by step 3. The identity transformation of the latter equality has itself as inverse and the constant $2$-simplices as its witnesses. The functor-equivalence definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] therefore proves the asserted equivalence of $p$. No step used filteredness or a chosen vertex of $I$. If $I$ is empty all maps out of $K=\varnothing$ in these formulas are the unique empty maps, so the same witnesses and identities still apply.
